changes.text: For BASE II-connected clients, charges for transactions that are settled in an Area Net Settlement Service (ANSS) is settled within the ANSS or within the International Settlement Service, depending on the rules of the ANSS. This table shows the charges reported for these two scenarios.

Visa Charges Report (VSS–140)—This report is used for the International Settlement Service, which lists all charges assessed on cross-border transactions settled in the International Settlement Service or charges assessed on cross-border transactions settled in the ANSS. Visa Charges Reconciliation Report (VSS–230)—This report is used for the Area Net Settlement Service, which lists only charges assessed on cross-border transactions settled in the ANSS. Note:  All cross-border charges are settled in the International Settlement Service.

This table shows the charges reported for these two scenarios.

The International Settlement Service that lists only charges assessed on transactions settled in the International Settlement Service. The NNSS that lists only charges assessed on transactions settled in the NNSS.

Visa Charges Report (VSS–140)—This report is used for the International Settlement Service, which lists all charges assessed on transactions settled in the International Settlement Service and the NNSS or ANSS. Visa Charges Reconciliation Report (VSS–230)—This report is used for the National Net or Area Net Settlement Services, which lists only charges assessed on transactions settled in the NNSS or ANSS, but settled in the International Settlement Service.

changes.old: U.S. clients that do not have their own VisaNet Access Point (VAP) endpoint (that decide to settle for themselves) are billed a monthly charge for funds transfers. The charge is intended to offset the added expense for Visa to send settlement wires to those that want to settle directly with Visa. The monthly charge is billed through the Billing Statement. There is no charge for the primary VisaNet funds transfer point (usually the VAP-connected processor if the processor is a funds transfer point). Clients that settle for themselves should also expect to receive wire charges from their settlement banks. All U.S. clients are billed monthly for nonfinancial transaction processing charges, which include a charge for each report generation record and for each item of clients settlement data. These charges also apply to report generation records and each item of client settlement data for any summary- level settlement reporting entities (SREs) that the client establishes. See Visa U.S.A. Inc. Operating Regulations, Volume 1—General Rules

If the machine-readable (TC 46) format is to be requested, clients must test the receipt of the data.
